newsitem.title: GERMANY: German GSA Aerotrans re-structures after MBO.
newsitem.headline: German GSA Aerotrans re-structures after MBO.

text.p: Germany's largest cargo general sales agent, Aerotrans Luftfahrtagentur GmbH, is re-structuring following a management buy-out earlier this year.

Aerotrans sales manager Germany, Lothar Schaller, said in an interview the GSA is targeting load factor improvement and new services aiming to become an all-round local freight agent in the medium-term..
Already a new capacity management department has boosted load factors of Frankfurt departures and will operate Germany-wide within three months.
"What we want to do is to improve capacity marketing on each flight and in the last three months we have achieved substantial sales," Schaller said.
"We expect an average load factor improvement of 15 percent this year," he added.
Managing director Hartmut Gunnemann led the buy-out after Aerotrans founder Helge Luehr decided to sell the agency.
A central sales and marketing department has been established and regional managers for central, southern and northern Germany appointed.
"We are moving away from branches. We are trying to concentrate administration but decentralise sales in the six branch offices," he explained.
Aerotrans has branches in Frankfurt, Stuttgart, Munich, Duesseldorf, Hamburg and Berlin.
Aerotrans had a turnover of 47.5 million marks and handled 20,000 tonnes of air cargo in 1995, up 20 percent from 1994, Schaller said.
Aerotrans is the German GSA for more than 15 carriers including USAir, LanChile, Air Namibia and Asiana Airlines and has already provided documentation handling for several clients.
Schaller said Aerotrans is watching the development of the physical handling sector "with interest" -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
